chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Rifa'ah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
If he is in snow, then let him look to the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something dusty.

So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the way to reconcile them is that it is obligatory upon a person to rub himself with snow or ice, since it is water, when that is possible for him and he does not fear for himself from using it; and he should not turn away from that to tayammum with earth and dust.

But if that is not possible for him, and he fears for himself from using it, then it is permissible for him to turn to tayammum, just as it is permissible for him to turn from water to earth in the presence of fear. And that which indicates this is what...

key_terms.الْجَمَدِ: ice, considered water in this legal context
key_terms.الْخَوْفِ: fear of harm, which permits turning from water to tayammum
key_terms.ثَلْجٍ: snow used in the discussion of purification
key_terms.غُبَارِهِ: its dust, used as material for tayammum
key_terms.لِبْدَ: the felt covering of a saddle from which dust may be taken
key_terms.مَاءٌ: water, the original means of purification
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمْ: to perform tayammum as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: When is tayammum allowed instead of using snow or ice for purification?
ai.summary: This text discusses the legal ruling for purification in conditions of snow and ice. It explains that snow and ice are treated as water when their use is possible and not harmful, but if using them endangers a person, then tayammum with dust becomes permissible.
